newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Widow of coup plot general leaves Morocco for France.
newsitem.headline: Widow of coup plot general leaves Morocco for France.

text.p: The widow of former Moroccan defence minister Mohamed Oufkir, who died after a failed coup against King Hassan in 1972, was to leave for France on Monday, the office of her lawyer said.
Fatima Oufkir had already left her home in Casablanca for the airport with her lawyer Mohamed Naciri, the lawyer's office said.
"Yes, she is leaving for France today," a spokeswoman said.
No official comment was immediately available.
Three of General Oufkir's children were allowed to fly to France last July after long being banned from leaving Morocco.

The general, a power behind the throne for years, was officially said to have committed suicide after Moroccan Air Force planes tried to shoot down the king's plane as it flew home from France in 1972. Opposition sources said he was summarily shot.
Fatima, six children and a relative were held in detention before being released in 1991 after a campaign by human rights groups. But they were banned from leaving Morocco.
